answer: The sable multiplier is published, charged in nectar, and copper lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 16 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 3600 identities would post 1936 proofs and burn roughly 6 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
